definitions.explanation: A position or boundary established to defend against attack. Used both literally in military and sports contexts, and figuratively for any boundary one tries to hold.

examples.japanese: {防御線|ぼうぎょせん}を{張|は}る。
examples.english: To set up a line of defense.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}の{攻撃|こうげき}で{防御線|ぼうぎょせん}が{崩|くず}れた。
examples.english: The defensive line collapsed under the enemy's attack.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}では、これ{以上|いじょう}{値下|ねさ}げしないという{防御線|ぼうぎょせん}を{守|まも}り{通|とお}した。
examples.english: In the negotiation, I held the line on not lowering the price any further.

notes:
Composed of {防御|ぼうぎょ} (defense, protection) + {線|せん} (line). Used literally for military positions and sports formations, and figuratively in business, politics, and daily life for any boundary one tries to maintain.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {防御線|ぼうぎょせん}を{張|は}る: to set up a defensive line
- {防御線|ぼうぎょせん}を{守|まも}る: to hold the defensive line
- {防御線|ぼうぎょせん}が{崩|くず}れる: for the defensive line to collapse
- {防御線|ぼうぎょせん}を{突破|とっぱ}する: to break through the defensive line
- {最後|さいご}の{防御線|ぼうぎょせん}: the last line of defense

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {防衛線|ぼうえいせん}: defense line — nearly synonymous; {防衛|ぼうえい} has a slightly more national/strategic nuance
- {守備|しゅび}ライン: defensive line (sports) — used in soccer, baseball, and other team sports
- {最終|さいしゅう}ライン: last line — the rearmost defensive position in sports
